name: Divadelní's cutting by the National Theatre, its east side
why: náměstí Václava Havla stands 3 m over the street in the cutting; the survey has the wall's top as a paved area's edge, not as a wall, and the plaza ran down to the street as a slope. North of here the stairs come down beside the wall

name: 5. května over Hvězdova at Pankrác, the west side of the underpass
why: 5. května and its slip roads cross Hvězdova on short bridges off embankments 6 m high; the survey has the embankment's top edge (264 m) but no wall, and the ground under the bridges ran up to it as a torn slope with the guardrails in zigzags. The low ground there is too wide for the cutting rule (CUT_RISE) to see the slope

name: 5. května over Hvězdova at Pankrác, the east side of the underpass
why: as the west side: the embankment's top edge (265 m) along the far side of the low ground under the bridges, carried on north-east along the lattice's step
